column1: # Windows Services Manager - "can this service be disabled?" advice
#   caution = disable only if you don't use the feature described
#   safe    = usually safe to disable for home PCs
# The app downloads this file from GitHub; edit it here to update the advice.

column3: Remote Procedure Call is the core of Windows: almost everything depends on it. Windows will not work without it.
Resolves RPC connections for other services. Windows will not work properly without it.
Starts COM and DCOM components. Windows will not work without it.
Local Session Manager handles sign-in sessions. Windows will not work without it.
Security Accounts Manager: needed for signing in and for security.
Detects and configures hardware. Without it, devices stop working.
Manages power settings and sleep. Needed by Windows.
Coordinates background tasks for Windows and apps. Needed by Windows.
Delivers system events to background tasks. Needed by Windows.
Communication between Windows components. Disabling it can break the desktop.
Windows Event Log. Needed for logging and by many services; disabling it causes errors elsewhere.
COM+ Event System. Many services depend on it.
System Event Notification: tells apps about sign-in, network and power changes.
User Profile Service: without it you cannot sign in.
Group Policy Client: applies system settings and policies.
Windows Management Instrumentation: used by Windows, drivers and many programs.
Cryptographic Services: needed for Windows Update, signatures and secure connections.
Gets your IP address from the router. Without it, most networks stop working.
DNS Client: turns web addresses into IP addresses. Needed for the internet.
Network Store Interface: needed for networking.
Network Location Awareness: identifies networks. Many network features depend on it.
Network List Service: needed by the network settings and many apps.
Windows Connection Manager: picks network connections automatically.
Base Filtering Engine: needed by Windows Firewall and IPsec. Disabling it lowers security.
Windows Defender Firewall. Keep it on for security.
Microsoft Defender Antivirus. Keep it unless another antivirus has replaced it (Windows handles that automatically).
Microsoft Defender network inspection: part of your antivirus protection.
Windows Security service: reports the health of your protection.
Security Center: monitors antivirus, firewall and update status.
Task Scheduler: Windows and many programs rely on scheduled tasks.
User Manager: needed for multi-user features and signing in.
State Repository: needed by the Start menu and Store apps.
Time Broker: runs background tasks for apps on schedule.
Application Information: needed for "Run as administrator" (UAC). Disabling it breaks elevation.
CNG Key Isolation: protects private keys used by Windows and Wi-Fi.
Credential Manager: stores saved passwords for Windows and apps.
Windows Audio Endpoint Builder: without it there is no sound.
Windows Audio: without it there is no sound.
Themes: provides the Windows look. Disabling it makes Windows look and behave oddly.
Display Policy: manages displays and scaling.
Device Install Service: needed to install new hardware.
Windows Modules Installer: needed to install updates and Windows features.
Windows Update: keeps Windows secure. Pause updates in Settings instead of disabling this.
Update Orchestrator: schedules Windows Update. Disabling it stops security updates.
Windows Update Medic: repairs Windows Update. Windows protects it from being disabled.
Background Intelligent Transfer: downloads Windows updates and app updates in the background.
Software Protection: Windows activation. Disabling it can mark Windows as not activated.
Workstation: needed to open shared folders and network drives.
WinHTTP Web Proxy Auto-Discovery: needed for proxies and some network features.
Web Account Manager: needed to sign in to Microsoft and work accounts in apps.
Microsoft Passport: needed for Windows Hello PIN sign-in.
Microsoft Passport Container: needed for Windows Hello PIN sign-in.
Capability Access Manager: controls which apps can use the camera, microphone and location.
App Readiness: prepares apps when you first sign in or after updates.
BitLocker Drive Encryption: needed if any drive is encrypted with BitLocker.
Optimize Drives: trims SSDs and defragments hard disks on schedule. Keep it for disk health and speed.
Windows Installer: needed to install, repair and remove programs. It only runs when needed.
Shell Hardware Detection: AutoPlay when you insert USB drives, discs or cameras. Disable only if you don't want AutoPlay.
Clipboard User Service: clipboard history and cloud clipboard (Win+V).
Connected User Experiences and Telemetry sends diagnostic and usage data to Microsoft. Disabling it does not affect normal use.
Device Management WAP Push routes management messages for company-managed (MDM) PCs. Home PCs don't need it.
Downloaded Maps Manager: only used by the Maps app for offline maps.
Retail Demo Service: only for display PCs in shops.
Fax: only needed if you send or receive faxes with this PC.
Remote Registry lets other computers change this PC's registry. Disabling it is recommended for security.
Windows Media Player network sharing: only needed to share your media library on the network.
Windows Error Reporting sends crash reports to Microsoft. Programs still work without it.
Problem Reports control panel support. Not needed for normal use.
Program Compatibility Assistant suggests fixes for old programs. Safe to disable on most PCs.
Windows Insider Service: only needed if you are in the Windows Insider program.
Payments and NFC/SE Manager: only for NFC payments on devices that support them.
AllJoyn Router: for some smart-home devices; almost nobody needs it.
Application Layer Gateway: only used with Internet Connection Sharing.
Infrared monitor: only for infrared (IrDA) devices.
Net.Tcp Port Sharing: only used by some developer and server software. Disabled by default.
Routing and Remote Access: for using the PC as a router. Disabled by default.
SNMP Trap: for network management systems in companies.
Peer Networking Grouping: rarely used peer-to-peer feature.
Peer Networking Identity Manager: rarely used peer-to-peer feature.
Peer Name Resolution Protocol: rarely used peer-to-peer feature.
PNRP Machine Name Publication: rarely used peer-to-peer feature.
Link-Layer Topology Discovery Mapper: draws the network map; rarely used.
Windows Connect Now: old Wi-Fi setup method (WPS). Rarely used.
Microsoft Windows SMS Router: text messaging for phone-linked or cellular PCs.
iSCSI Initiator: only for connecting to iSCSI storage, mostly in companies.
BranchCache: a company network feature.
Diagnostics Hub collector: used by developer tools such as Visual Studio.
Wallet Service: rarely used by apps.
Windows Event Collector: collects events from other PCs; used in companies.
Auto Time Zone Updater: sets the time zone from your location. Disabled by default.
Windows Perception Service: only for mixed-reality headsets.
Windows Mixed Reality OpenXR: only for mixed-reality headsets.
Spatial Data Service: only for mixed-reality features.
OpenSSH Authentication Agent: only needed if you use SSH keys. Disabled by default.
Messaging Service: text messaging support; rarely needed.
Recommended Troubleshooting Service: offers automatic troubleshooters.
Windows Push Notifications: needed for app notifications and live tiles. Disable only if you don't want notifications.
Windows Push Notifications (user): needed for app notifications. Disable only if you don't want notifications.
Offline Files: only needed if you use offline copies of network folders.
Distributed Link Tracking Client: keeps shortcuts working across network drives; rarely needed at home.
TCP/IP NetBIOS Helper: needed by older network file sharing and some NAS drives.
SysMain (Superfetch) preloads frequently used programs. It helps on hard disks; on fast SSDs disabling it has little effect.
Windows Search indexes files so searching in Start, Explorer and Outlook is fast. Disabling it makes search slow.
Print Spooler is needed for any printing, including "Print to PDF". Disable only if you never print.
Printer Extensions and Notifications: shows printer status and settings. Needed if you print.
Geolocation: lets Windows and apps find your location (weather, maps, Find my device).
Touch Keyboard and Handwriting: also needed for the emoji panel and typing in some apps. Keep it on touch devices.
Bluetooth Support: needed for any Bluetooth device (mouse, headphones, phone).
Bluetooth Audio Gateway: needed for Bluetooth headsets with a microphone.
AVCTP: needed for Bluetooth headphone controls.
Windows Biometric Service: needed for Windows Hello fingerprint and face sign-in.
Smart Card: only needed if you use a smart card or a smart-card reader.
Smart Card Device Enumeration: only needed with smart cards.
Smart Card Removal Policy: only needed with smart cards.
Phone Service: telephony and Phone Link calls.
Telephony: used by some VPN, dial-up and fax software.
Parental Controls: needed for Microsoft Family Safety on child accounts.
Windows Mobile Hotspot: needed to share this PC's connection as a hotspot.
Internet Connection Sharing: needed for Mobile Hotspot and sharing a connection.
Wi-Fi Direct: needed for wireless displays (Miracast) and some printers.
Windows Image Acquisition: needed for scanners and some cameras.
Still Image Acquisition Events: starts apps when you press a scanner or camera button.
Remote Desktop Services: needed to connect to this PC with Remote Desktop.
Remote Desktop Device Redirector: needed for Remote Desktop printers and drives.
Remote Desktop Configuration: needed for Remote Desktop.
Windows Remote Management: used by PowerShell remoting and management tools.
Secondary Logon: needed for "Run as a different user".
Server: shares this PC's files and printers on the network. Disable only if you never share.
SSDP Discovery: finds network devices such as media servers, smart TVs and printers.
UPnP Device Host: lets this PC act as a network media device.
Function Discovery Resource Publication: makes this PC visible on the network.
Function Discovery Provider Host: needed to see other PCs and devices on the network.
WebClient: needed to open WebDAV folders such as some SharePoint sites.
IP Helper: IPv6 transition technologies; some VPNs and games need it.
Quality Windows Audio Video Experience: improves streaming quality on home networks.
Diagnostic Policy Service: Windows troubleshooters and problem detection need it.
Diagnostic Service Host: used by Windows troubleshooters.
Diagnostic System Host: used by Windows troubleshooters.
Data Usage: tracks data use and metered connections. Needed for data limits.
Portable Device Enumerator: needed for phones, cameras and media players over USB.
Radio Management: Airplane mode and radio switches.
Windows Time keeps the clock correct. A wrong clock breaks secure websites and sign-in.
Cellular Time: sets the clock from the mobile network on cellular PCs.
Volume Shadow Copy: needed for System Restore points and many backup programs.
Microsoft Software Shadow Copy Provider: needed for System Restore and backups.
Windows Backup: needed for Windows' own backup.
Block Level Backup Engine: needed for Windows system image backups.
Virtual Disk: needed by Disk Management and partition tools.
Encrypting File System: needed if you use encrypted files or folders.
Font Cache: speeds up programs by caching fonts. Disabling it can slow apps down.
Sensor Service: screen rotation, auto-brightness and other sensors.
Sensor Monitoring: auto-brightness and screen rotation on laptops and tablets.
Sensor Data Service: delivers sensor data to apps.
Device Setup Manager: installs drivers and apps for new devices.
Connected Devices Platform: needed for Phone Link, Nearby sharing and Bluetooth features.
Connected Devices Platform (user): needed for Phone Link and Nearby sharing.
Delivery Optimization: downloads updates efficiently, also from other PCs. Limit it in Settings instead of disabling it.
Microsoft Store Install Service: needed to install and update Store apps.
Client License Service: needed by Microsoft Store apps. Disabling it can stop Store apps from opening.
AppX Deployment: installs and updates Store apps.
Windows License Manager: needed by Microsoft Store apps.
Microsoft Account Sign-in Assistant: needed to sign in with a Microsoft account.
Netlogon: needed on PCs joined to a company domain.
KtmRm for Distributed Transaction Coordinator: used by some database and business software.
Distributed Transaction Coordinator: used by some database and business software.
Contact Data: contacts search for Mail, People and Phone Link.
User Data Storage: stores contacts, calendar and mail for the built-in apps.
User Data Access: gives apps access to contacts, calendar and mail.
Sync Host: syncs mail, contacts and calendar.
Xbox Live Auth Manager: needed for Xbox and Game Pass games. Disable only if you don't play them.
Xbox Live Game Save: syncs game saves. Disable only if you don't play Xbox or Game Pass games.
Xbox Live Networking: needed for online Xbox games.
Xbox Accessory Management: needed for Xbox controllers.
GameInput Service: needed by some games for controllers.
Hyper-V Host: only needed if you run Hyper-V virtual machines.
Hyper-V Data Exchange: only needed inside Hyper-V virtual machines.
Hyper-V Guest Service Interface: only needed inside Hyper-V virtual machines.
Hyper-V Guest Shutdown: only needed inside Hyper-V virtual machines.
Hyper-V Heartbeat: only needed inside Hyper-V virtual machines.
Hyper-V PowerShell Direct: only needed inside Hyper-V virtual machines.
Hyper-V Remote Desktop Virtualization: only needed inside Hyper-V virtual machines.
Hyper-V Time Synchronization: only needed inside Hyper-V virtual machines.
Hyper-V Volume Shadow Copy Requestor: only needed inside Hyper-V virtual machines.
Microsoft Edge Update: keeps Edge secure. Disabling it stops Edge security updates.
Microsoft Edge Update: keeps Edge secure. Disabling it stops Edge security updates.
Google Update: keeps Chrome secure. Disabling it stops Chrome security updates.
Google Update: keeps Chrome secure. Disabling it stops Chrome security updates.
Mozilla Maintenance: lets Firefox update silently. Firefox can still update itself while open.
Adobe Acrobat Update: keeps Adobe Reader secure.
OpenSSH Server: only needed to connect to this PC over SSH.
World Wide Web Publishing (IIS): only needed if this PC hosts websites.
Windows Process Activation: needed by IIS web hosting.
Warp JIT: used by some graphics features in apps.
Inventory and Compatibility Appraisal: checks app compatibility for Windows upgrades and sends data to Microsoft.
Windows Health and Optimized Experiences: sends health data to improve suggestions.
Now Playing Session Manager: media controls on the volume flyout and lock screen.
System Guard Runtime Monitor: part of Windows security.
Windows Firewall driver.
